welcome.heading: Welcome to Streaming Tree for OBS
welcome.flow: OBS sends one stream to Streaming Tree for OBS, which distributes it to your destinations - Twitch, YouTube, Kick, TikTok - and powers chat, alerts, overlays and other engagement tools alongside it.
welcome.standalone: Streaming Tree is a standalone companion application, not an OBS plugin. It never modifies your OBS installation or its configuration files - OBS simply points one output at it, like any other streaming destination.
welcome.expectation: This short assistant explains what to check and where to find it. You can skip it at any time and reopen it later from Settings.

readiness.heading: Local streaming engine
readiness.body: Streaming Tree needs its local ingest engine and a compatible FFmpeg to actually stream. Here's what's ready right now.

obsConnection.heading: Connect OBS
obsConnection.body: Point OBS at Streaming Tree with these values.

steps.pasteValues: Paste the Server and Stream Key values below.

destinations.heading: Destinations
destinations.body: Destinations are where your stream is sent - Twitch, YouTube, Kick, TikTok. You don't need any configured yet to finish this assistant.

accounts.heading: Connected accounts
accounts.distinction: A connected account is different from a destination: a destination is where your video is sent, while a connected account authorizes chat, events and other account-aware features. You don't need one to stream.

creatorTools.heading: Creator tools
creatorTools.body: Streaming Tree also powers chat, alerts, goals and audio alongside your stream. A quick look at what's already available.
creatorTools.noOverlayYet: You don't have a chat overlay yet.

summary.heading: You're ready to go
summary.body: Setup is complete. You can always come back to this assistant from Settings if you want a refresher.
